title: "Data"

## Inputs

| input | source | vintage | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| building footprints + heights | GlobalBuildingAtlas (TU Munich, PlanetScope-derived) | 2024 | 673,583 raw; height error 1.5–9 m |
| building typology | Overture Maps POI matching | 2026 | 12 classes; ~35% evidence-supported, rest heuristic |
| slum extents | mapped slums (KML) | 2016 | 2,542 polygons, 33.5 km² |
| ward boundaries | BMC / open data | — | 24 wards |
| ward population | MCGM civic demographics | mid-2023 | 13,014,389 |
| income proxy | Maharashtra Annual Statement of Rates via public compilations | 2026–27 | 125 localities → ward medians |
| weather | daily Tmax/Tmin | 1951–2024 | station era only (2020+) |
| road network | OpenStreetMap via osmnx | 2026 | 6,157 km |

## Derived stock

```{python}
import geopandas as gpd, pandas as pd
s = gpd.read_parquet("data/interim/stock_population.parquet")
pd.DataFrame({
    "buildings in Greater Mumbai": [f"{len(s):,}"],
    "floor area": [f"{s.floor_area_m2.sum()/1e6:.1f} km²"],
    "households": [f"{s.households.sum()/1e6:.2f} M"],
    "informal share of buildings": [f"{100*s.is_slum.mean():.1f}%"],
}).T.rename(columns={0: ""})
```

## The income proxy

The eASR portal disallows automated access, so ward-level rates were derived from published
compilations of the same official schedule: 125 revenue-village localities, manually mapped
to wards with a confidence flag, then taken as a median per ward. The spread is 7.3× from
M/East (₹53,970/m²) to A ward (₹3,92,624/m²), which is enough to define four meaningful
income bands.

It remains **land value, not income**. Its worst failure — informal settlements inside
expensive wards, such as Dharavi in G/North or Behrampada in H/East — is handled by pinning
slum-flagged buildings to the lowest band regardless of rate.

## The weather record

The daily series splices two sources, visible in the decimal precision: 1951–2019 is a
gridded product (April–May median Tmax ≈ 35.9 °C, daily range ≈ 12 °C), 2020–2024 is
station data (34.5 °C, range ≈ 8.5 °C). The gridded era is inland-biased and would
overstate cooling demand, so only the station era is used. A typical pre-monsoon day is
taken as the April–May median and expanded to 24 hours with a Parton–Logan curve.

One consequence: a single series means **no urban heat island gradient**. Every ward
receives identical forcing, and the only spatial variation in indoor temperature comes from
building fabric.
